 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

2. Briefly stated, the case of the petitioner is as follows:
That on 05.09.2020 at about 6.00 p.m. when the petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 05-HS-4510 and when he reached near Bejjarahallikatte,
at that time the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z- 1763 came from Magadi side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle .
As a result, petitioner fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
He took treatment in Narayana Hospital and then in Ramakrishna hospital.
A case was registered in Crime No.274/2020 against the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 at Ramanagara Rural police station.

Hence,
this petition for compensation.
3. In response to the notice of the petition, the respondents have appeared before the Court through their respective counsels and have filed their written statement separately.
The respondent No.1 has denied the entire averments of the petition as false.
The alleged accident has been occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself .

He has admitted that he is the registered owner of the Suzuki Baleno car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 and it has been insured with the 2nd respondent and the policy was valid from 09.02.2020 to 08.02.2021 and the same was in force as on the date of accident.
The driver of the car had valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
4. The second respondent in its written statement has denied the petition averments as false.
It has also denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-06-Z-1763.
The driver of the car had no valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The owner of the vehicle knowingly was driving the car without having valid and effective driving licence and it amounts to clear violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.

The car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 was not involved in the alleged accident and it was intentionally implicated in collusion with the driver, owner and other authorities to get unlawful benefit from the insurance company.
The petitioner was riding the the motorcycle unmindfully and without observing the traffic and hence, petitioner himself was the architect of the accident.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 05.09.2020 at about 6.00 p.m. near Bejjarallikatte, Kutgal Hobli, Ramanagara-Magadi Road, Ramanagara, within the jurisdiction of Ramanagara Rural police station on account of rash and negligent driving of the car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 by its driver when the petitioner was riding the two wheeler bearing reg. No.KA-05-HS-4510?
2. Whether the 1st respondent proves that the accident has occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of petitioner himself?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order?
6. On behalf of the petitioner, he examined himself as PW-1 and one witness is examined as PW2 and got marked Exhibits P.1 to P.20.
The respondent No.2 has not led any evidence either oral or documentary.
7. Heard the arguments of both sides.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... In the negative Issue No.3 ...

Partly in affirmative, awarding compensation of Rs.26,50,600/ -
Issue No.4 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue Nos.1 and 2 :- Since these issues involve common discussion, I have taken them together.

The petitioner in order to prove his case has placed reliance on his oral evidence and documentary evidence as per Exs.P.1 to P. 7 such as FIR , complaint, chargesheet , panchanama, wound certificate, discharge summary and IMV report.

PW-1 being the injured, in his affidavit evidence has narrated how he met with an accident and the accident was due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-06- Z-1763 .
The respondents No.1 and 2 have filed written statement by denying the accident and also the negligence aspect.
Both of them have taken the contention that accident has occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.

The second respondent has contended that the car in question was not at all involved in the alleged accident, but it was intentionally implicated in collusion with the driver , owner and police to get unlawful gain from the insurance company.

Let us consider the evidence placed by the petitioner to Puttaraju B vs Aravinda T.S on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113167410/
3 decide these issues.

10. As per PW1 on 05.09.2020 at about 6.00 p.m. when he was riding motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 05-HS-4510 near Bejjarahallikate, Kootgal hobli , Ramanagar district, at that time the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 came from Magadi side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to his vehicle and thereby he fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
Accident occurred on 05.09.2020 and the complaint was lodged on the same day by the petitioner.

Even in the complaint the petitioner has stated the manner in which he met with an accident on account of rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763.
On the basis of the complaint lodged by the petitioner, a criminal case was registered against the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763.
PW 1 was cross
- examined by the second respondent counsel, but nothing worth is elicited from his mouth to disbelieve his evidence, as to the car in question causing accident to him.
Nowhere in the cross-examination of PW1, it was suggested that the car was not at all involved in the accident and the said car has not caused accident to him.
Absolutely there are no suggestions in respect of the negligence aspect on the part of the petitioner in occurring of the accident.
11. Panchanama as per Ex.P.4 reveals the state of affairs at the accident spot.

As per Ex.P.4 the place of accident is near tank bund of Bejjerahallikatte situated at Ramanagar - Magadi road and the width of the said road is 22 feet and it runs North to South and by the side of the said road there are footpaths.
The petitioner has not produced the sketch before the Court.

However, as PW1 was not cross-examined by the second respondent counsel by making suggestions as to occurring of the accident on account of rash and negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself, the non-production of the sketch do not assume much importance.
12. In Ex.P.4 it is mentioned that both the vehicles involved in the accident were seized at the time of mahazar and also the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
Ex.P.7 is the IMV Report wherein the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
As per Ex.P.7 the front right side corner bumper of car was dent, front both side doors are damaged and pressed inwards and front both side wheel out off fixture due to impact.
The front head light doom of the motorcycle was broken, right side fuel tank dent , right side crash guard scratched, rear right side body shield broken, rear wheel out off fixture due to impact.

By considering the damages mentioned in Exhibits P.4 and P.7, it can be said that it is the driver of the car who came from Magadi side has hit the motorcycle of the petitioner resulting in the damages to both the vehicles.

Hence, from these documents, it can be safely held that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763.
13.
Wound certificate Ex.P.5 discloses that the petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and two simple injuries in accident.
Ex.P.3 is the chargesheet filed against the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-06- Z-1763 after detailed investigation by the police.
This driver is no other than the owner of the car and he is the first respondent in the case.
Except filing the written statement by the first respondent in denying the accident and negligence aspect , he has not chosen to place his evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Mere taking contention in the written statement itself is not sufficient, unless it is proved by placing cogent evidence.

Moreover, it is noticed that the first Puttaraju B vs Aravinda T.S on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113167410/
4 respondent being the driver of the car in question has not challenged the chargesheet filed against him.
This conduct of the first respondent enables the Court to draw an adverse inference against him that as accident took place due to his negligence, he has remained silent.
Even the second respondent has not chosen to prove the non-involvement of the car in question and also the negligence of the petitioner in occurring of the accident.
Thus, absolutely, there is no evidence on behalf of the respondents to prove their contentions.

Hence, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved that accident took place due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763, whereas the first respondent has failed to prove that accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the petitioner himself.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative and Issue No.2 in the negative.

14. ISSUE No.2:
(a). Pain and Agony:

PW-1 has produced the wound Certificate at Ex.P.5, which discloses that the petitioner has sustained (1) Tenderness over the lumbar region, swelling , movements restricted, (2) abrasion over the right leg, (3) abrasion over the left ankle.
X-ray shows burst fracture.
As per the opinion of the doctor injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injuries No.2 and 3 are simple in nature.
Discharge summary-Ex.P.6 and inpatient record as per Ex.P.15
discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment in Ramakrishna hospital as an inpatient from 05.09.2020 to 18.09.2020.
As per the doctor -PW2 and as per medical records, the petitioner underwent Decompression L-1 to L- 5 posterior lumbar interbody fusion on 09.09.2020.
As per PW2, recent x-ray shows malunited fracture of L-3 with implants in situ.
PW1 has deposed that he is still under treatment as outpatient and he has produced out patient record as per Ex.P.16.
Ex.P.16 is in respect of further treatment taken by the petitioner on account of the complications suffered by him due to the accidental injuries.
Exhibits P.17 and P.18 are the x-rays which confirms that the petitioner has sustained L3 burst fracture with traumatic paraplegia.
PW1 in his cross-examination has deposed that after 1 year 3 months from the date of discharge from Ramakrishna hospital, he was readmitted in Supra hospital, Bengaluru.

As per his admission he was admitted to the said hospital with reference to right leg knee injury and at that time of using walker as per the advise of doctor, he fell down and same history was mentioned in Ex.P.9, which is the discharge summary of Supra hospital.

In Ex.P.9 it is mentioned that the petitioner suffers from traumatic paraplegia more at right leg since 1 year 3 months and when he was walking with walker on 04.01.2022 at 4.00 p.m. he suddenly slipped and fell down and sustained injury to right knee.
The medical records of Ramakrishna hospital disclose that the petitioner had sustained burst fracture L3 with paraplegia.
As such, it can be said that the petitioner was not in a position to walk independently without the support of the walker.

Ex. P.9 - discharge summary of Supra hospital,
Bengaluru discloses that the petitioner was admitted to the said hospital on 04.01.2022 on account of his slipping suddenly at the time of walking with a walker.

Hence, it can be said that the right knee dislocation with popliteal artery injury sustained by the petitioner is on account of petitioner Puttaraju B vs Aravinda T.S on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113167410/
5 not being able to walk on account of traumatic paraplegia.

The injuries sustained by the petitioner requires 7 months treatment.
During the treatment period, the petitioner has suffered lot of pain and agony.

So, taking into account the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and number of days of his treatment in the hospital, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head Pain and agony.

(b). Medical Expenses (including conveyance, attendant charges and extra nourishment):
PW-1 has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical treatment and surgery, Rs.1,00,000/- towards food and nourishment, Rs.2,50,000/-
towards attendant charges and Rs.80,000/- towards travelling expenses.

The medical records disclose that the petitioner has taken treatment in Supra hospital as an inpatient from 04.01.2022 to 15.01.2022 for the injury sustained on account of accidental injuries.
As such, it can be said that the petitioner has spent amount mentioned in Ex.P.12(1).
In Ex.P.12(2) is the pharmacy bill amounting to to Rs.75,692/-.
This medical bill is not supported by any prescription.
However, the charges of medicines prescribed to the petitioner while he was in Supra hospital is not shown in Ex.P.12.
Hence, it can be said that the petitioner has spent the said amount towards medicines while he was inpatient in Supra hospital.
In Ex.P.12, bills of Ramakrishna hospital are produced.

The petitioner is entitled for these amounts.
The petitioner has produced pharmacy bills of S.S.Pharma which do not contain the signature of the person who has issued them and seal of the shop.
The pharmacy bills are not supported by prescriptions.
Hence, it can be said that the petitioner has not spent the amount claimed under the pharmacy bills.

However, by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and type of treatment undergone by him, it can be said that the petitioner has spent some amount towards medicines, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges in both Ramakrishna hospital and Supra hospital.
Ex.P.12(26) is an Ambulance bill and Ex.P.12(27) is the blood donated bill .
Petitioner is entitled for the said amounts.

By considering these facts, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has spent amounts towards hospital charges,

Hence, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.5,67,000/- under this head.
(c) Loss of income during the treatment period:

PW-1 has deposed that, prior to the accident he was doing agriculture and dairy farming and he was earning Rs.20,000/p.m., but due to the accident he was unable to do any work and he has suffered loss of income.

Except the oral assertion of PW1,
no material is placed in proof of his avocation and income.

In the absence of evidence, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as per the Minimum Wages Act in view of the judgment of the Division Bench of our own High Court in MFA No.7404/2014 (Smt.Mariyamma and others Vs Sri Suyambulingam and another), dated 06.12.2022.

As per the Minimum Wages Act, the income of the petitioner has to be taken at Rs.10,000/p.m.
Injuries sustained by the petitioner requires minimum 7 months treatment.
During that period petitioner was unable to do any work.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.70,000/- under this head.
(d) Future loss of earning capacity:

PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he has suffered paraparesis, lost lower sensation in both lower limbs, he lost control over below waist with paralysis of both lower limb and lost control over urinal on passing sense and his life has become miserable and he cannot do his agricultural work and dairy farming.
He has suffered paraplegia and without the help of others he cannot get up from the bed, attend nature call, have food properly and he has suffered regular stomach infection.
In order to prove the disability the petitioner has examined the Doctor of Ramakrishna Hospital as PW2.
PW2 in his evidence has deposed about the injuries suffered by the petitioner and the line of treatment given.
As per PW2, he has assessed the disability and petitioner suffers from permanent physical impairment to the whole body at 55%.
Whether the disability assessed by PW2 is to be accepted or not has to be scrutinized cautiously.

PW2 in his cross-examination has deposed that he has given treatment to the petitioner in Ramakrishna hospital from 05.09.2020 to 18.09.2020 for L3 vertebral fracture with paralysis of both lower limbs with bowel and bladder paralysis sustained on account of accident.

PW2 has deposed that at the time of discharge also,
the petitioner was still paralysed.

PW2 has assessed the disability by observing traumatic paraparesis- Cauda Equina syndrome , malunited fracture of L3 body with implants in situ and total loss of bowel and bladder control and even recent x-ray showed malunion of the fracture of L3 .

The medical records disclose that the Puttaraju B vs Aravinda T.S on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113167410/
7 petitioner has sustained burst fracture L3 vertebra with traumatic paraplegia and subsequently he has sustained right knee dislocation with popliteal artery injury on account of his fall while walking with a walker and this condition of the petitioner was due to the accidental injuries suffered by him.
As PW2 is a treated Doctor, his evidence has to be believed to consider the disability assessed by him.
Though PW2 was cross-examined by the second respondent counsel, but nothing worth is elicited from his mouth to disbelieve the disability stated by him.
PW2 has admitted that by undergoing physiotherapy treatment and by undergoing rehabitation treatment , the disability stated by him may come down.
He has also admitted that spinal cord injury is neurological complications.
The petitioner was an agriculturist and Milk vendor.
Hence, by considering the avocation of the petitioner, the disability assessed by PW-2 will definitely reduce the earning capacity of the petitioner in his life.
As such by considering the avocation of the petitioner, the functional disability is taken at 60%.

In this regard I intend to rely upon a decision reported in 2014 ACJ 627 (Syed Sqdiq and Others Vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co., Ltd.,) wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India assessed the income at Rs.6,500/- per month for a vegetable vendor and assessed the permanent functional disability at 85% and added 50% income for future prospects and also awarded compensation on other heads such as cost of artificial leg, for pain and suffering, for loss of expectation of life, loss of amenities in life, for medical and incidental expenses and litigation costs.
According to the petitioner he was aged 24 years at the time of accident. PW-1 has produced his DL and Aadhar Card as per Exs.P.13 and 14, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 10.07.1994.

Depending upon the said age, as per the ratio laid down in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarala Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation) the proper multiplier applicable is 17.

As the petitioner is 26 years,
40% future prospects has to be added to his monthly income.
Therefore, 40% of Rs.10,000/- is Rs.4,000/-, monthly income is Rs.14,000/-.
The annual income of the petitioner comes to Rs.1,68,000/-.
As discussed above, the multiplier is 17.
If we multiply the annual income of the petitioner with 17 multiplier , the loss of future income comes to Rs.17,13,600/-.
As such, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.17,13,600/- under this head.
(e) Future Medical Expenses:

PW-1 has deposed that while operating the spinal cord injury implant has been inserted and as such doctor has advised him to undergo one more surgery which Puttaraju B vs Aravinda T.S on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113167410/

As such, the petitioner requires some amount towards future medical expenses.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- under the head future medical expenses which shall not carry any interest.

(f) Towards unhappiness and loss of amenities:
PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he has suffered paraparesis, lost lower sensation in both lower limbs, he lost control over below waist with paralysis of both lower limb and lost control over urinal on passing sense and his life has become miserable and he cannot do his agricultural work and dairy farming.
He has suffered paraplegia and without the help of others he cannot get up from the bed, attend nature call, have food properly and he has suffered regular stomach infection.

PW2 has deposed that petitioner suffers from traumatic paraparesis-Cauda Equina syndrome, fracture is malunited, there is total loss of bowel and bladder control and the petitioner suffers from permanent physical impairment to the whole body at 55%.
PW1 has produced the photos at Ex.P.10 which discloses that there are ugly scar marks at the injury site.
Even these ugly scar marks will cause unhappiness to the petitioner since it will give an ugly look.

From these difficulties stated by PWs 1 and 2,
it can be safely held that the petitioner suffered unhappiness and discomfort to some extent while doing his normal activities and avocation.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.1,50,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.26,50,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. excluding Rs.50,000/- awarded under the head of future medical expenses from the date of the petition till deposit in Court.
16. So far as the liability is concerned, according to the petitioner, the first respondent is the owner and the second respondent is the insurer of the car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 .

The first respondent in the written statement has admitted that he is the R.C.Owner of the said car and it has been insured with the second respondent under the policy and the policy was valid from 09.02.2020 to 08.02.2021.
The second respondent in the written statement has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z- 1763.
But the second respondent has not chosen to place any evidence in this regard.
The first respondent has produced the copy of the insurance policy standing in his name which discloses that the policy was valid from 9.02.2019 to 8.02.2022.
As such, the policy was valid as on the date of accident .

As discussed in issues No.1 and 2 , this Court has come to the conclusion that the petitioner has proved that he met with an accident on account of rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 .

Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount of Rs.26,50,600/- along with interest at 6% p.a. excluding Rs.50,000/- awarded under the head of future medical expenses from the date of the petition till deposit in Court.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.4 :

In view of my findings on Issue Nos.1 to 3 and for the reasons stated therein , I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER

The claim petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 and 2, awarding compensation of Rs.26,50,600/- (Rupees twenty six lakhs fifty thousand six hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a. excluding Rs.50,000/- awarded under the head of future medical expenses from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
As a result, petitioner fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
He took treatment in Narayana Hospital and then in Ramakrishna hospital.
A case was registered in Crime No.274/2020 against the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 at Ramanagara Rural police station.
Hence,
this petition for compensation.
The alleged accident has been occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself .
He has admitted that he is the registered owner of the Suzuki Baleno car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 and it has been insured with the 2nd respondent and the policy was valid from 09.02.2020 to 08.02.2021 and the same was in force as on the date of accident.
The driver of the car had valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed is excessive and exorbitant.
4. The second respondent in its written statement has denied the petition averments as false.
It has also denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-06-Z-1763.
The driver of the car had no valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The owner of the vehicle knowingly was driving the car without having valid and effective driving licence and it amounts to clear violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
The car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 was not involved in the alleged accident and it was intentionally implicated in collusion with the driver, owner and other authorities to get unlawful benefit from the insurance company.
The petitioner was riding the the motorcycle unmindfully and without observing the traffic and hence, petitioner himself was the architect of the accident.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 05.09.2020 at about 6.00 p.m. near Bejjarallikatte, Kutgal Hobli, Ramanagara-Magadi Road, Ramanagara, within the jurisdiction of Ramanagara Rural police station on account of rash and negligent driving of the car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763 by its driver when the petitioner was riding the two wheeler bearing reg. No.KA-05-HS-4510?
2. Whether the 1st respondent proves that the accident has occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of petitioner himself?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The second respondent has contended that the car in question was not at all involved in the alleged accident, but it was intentionally implicated in collusion with the driver , owner and police to get unlawful gain from the insurance company.
As the petitioner is 26 years,
40% future prospects has to be added to his monthly income.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Accident occurred on 05.09.2020 and the complaint was lodged on the same day by the petitioner.
Even in the complaint the petitioner has stated the manner in which he met with an accident on account of rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763.
On the basis of the complaint lodged by the petitioner, a criminal case was registered against the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-06-Z-1763.
This driver is no other than the owner of the car and he is the first respondent in the case.
Except filing the written statement by the first respondent in denying the accident and negligence aspect , he has not chosen to place his evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Mere taking contention in the written statement itself is not sufficient, unless it is proved by placing cogent evidence.
This conduct of the first respondent enables the Court to draw an adverse inference against him that as accident took place due to his negligence, he has remained silent.
Even the second respondent has not chosen to prove the non-involvement of the car in question and also the negligence of the petitioner in occurring of the accident.
In the absence of evidence, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as per the Minimum Wages Act in view of the judgment of the Division Bench of our own High Court in MFA No.7404/2014 (Smt.Mariyamma and others Vs Sri Suyambulingam and another), dated 06.12.2022.
This accident has occurred in the year 2020.
As per the Minimum Wages Act, the income of the petitioner has to be taken at Rs.10,000/p.m.
During that period petitioner was unable to do any work.
Hence, by considering the avocation of the petitioner, the disability assessed by PW-2 will definitely reduce the earning capacity of the petitioner in his life.
As such by considering the avocation of the petitioner, the functional disability is taken at 60%.
Depending upon the said age, as per the ratio laid down in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarala Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation) the proper multiplier applicable is 17.
